task_summary: Apply the 14 AUTHOR rulings, rework Appendix F, then hygienize the tracker

phases.name: Appendix F and the register law

steps.title: Read the appendix and all 15 author points
steps.description: Read apx_f_cosine.tex in full and the AUTHOR block in PENDENCIAS 2.22. Build a numbered checklist of the 15 points, each with the verbatim quote it targets and where that quote sits in the rendered PDF.

steps.title: Verify the two claims that need external sources
steps.description: Points 1 and 4 ask for a reference for the negative-transfer sentence and for the gradient-cosine measurement approach. Find each at source with a resolvable identifier and locate the specific supporting claim, or report NOT FOUND. Never invent a citation.

steps.title: Resolve the arc claim the author disputes
steps.description: Point 3 and point 13 say the first two studies used different tasks and a different architecture, so relating this appendix's result to them may be unsupportable. Measure what tasks and architecture each study used, then either scope the sentence to what holds or remove it.

steps.title: Apply the wording, cutting and simplification points
steps.description: Points 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 ask for cuts and plainer phrasing. Apply each, keeping every fact that the reader needs and moving the rest to source comments.

steps.title: Add the knowledge-sharing qualification
steps.description: Point 14 asks that F.3 note that gradients not adding up does not mean the tasks share no knowledge, since other mechanisms exist in the architecture. Add one sentence, grounded in what the model actually contains.

steps.title: Rename the appendix to D and verify
steps.description: The main volume prints A, C, E, F because B and D moved to the supplementary volume. Make the letters run A, B, C, D. Verify every cross-reference still resolves and no letter is hardcoded anywhere.

steps.title: Remove the sign-off marker and rebuild
steps.description: The author approves the appendix. Remove its NEEDS SIGN-OFF marker, rebuild all four targets, and verify each of the 15 points in the rendered PDF.

steps.title: Measure the British English present
steps.description: Sweep every live prose file for British spellings and usage with a validated instrument. Report counts per file and the exact hits.

steps.title: Write the British and hard-phrasing rules
steps.description: Add to WRITING_LAW the ban on British English and on constructions a non-native writer would not produce, using the author's own examples: feature needs saying plainly, two departures from that flat picture appear, both are worth reporting rather than smoothing.

steps.title: Build a gate for both classes
steps.description: Write a checker for British spellings and for the hard-phrasing shapes the author named. Validate in both directions against the real sentences, and wire it into check.sh.

steps.title: Fix every hit outside Appendix F
steps.description: Apply the fixes the sweep found in files other than apx_f_cosine, which the other track owns. Verify each in the rendered PDF.

phases.name: The remaining rulings and the tracker

steps.title: Apply the region-asymmetry ruling, option B
steps.description: The author chose to promote the TOST non-inferiority caveat in both the MobiWac manuscript and the dissertation frame prose, so both say four wins plus two non-inferior. Edit both trees and verify they stay identical.

steps.title: Apply the citation and banned-term rulings
steps.description: Items 2.15 and 2.14: substitute in both the original articles and add an errata row, and use the author-supplied BibTeX for the Nash-MTL page range. Verify each field against the source of record.

steps.title: Apply the remaining rulings
steps.description: Items 2.9, 2.12, 2.16, 2.18, 2.19, 2.20, 2.21 and 5.6b each carry a decision. Apply each, verify at source, and record what was measured.

steps.title: Apply the four approved RECOMMENDED
steps.description: Item 2.23: apply R-3, R-5, R-6 and EX-6 following the 42_excellence recommendation, and do not apply EX-9.

steps.title: Classify every tracker item by its own decision block
steps.description: Read each item's ask section rather than pattern-matching. Separate items that are closed, items still waiting on the author, and items that are records.

steps.title: Archive the closed items
steps.description: Move every closed item to PENDENCIAS_RESOLVIDOS with its outcome and evidence, repoint any source comment that cites a moved number, and confirm the orphan gate stays green.

steps.title: Retire section 4 if VERIFY_LIST is closed
steps.description: Verify whether the verification register is genuinely closed, and if so remove the section that points at it. If it is not closed, say what remains.

phases.name: Verify every requested change actually landed

steps.title: Build the ledger of every requested change
steps.description: Enumerate all 29 requested changes from source: the 14 AUTHOR rulings in PENDENCIAS §2 and §5, and the 15 numbered points in the 2.22 Appendix F block. One row each, with the verbatim text the author quoted and what he asked for. Take the rows from the tracker file, not from any track's report.

steps.title: Re-measure each row against the rendered PDF
steps.description: For every row, check the rendered document rather than the source, and never a track's self-report. Record APPLIED, NOT APPLIED, or REPORTED BLOCKED with the reason. Strip comments before judging prose, search across line wraps, and prove each pattern can find its target when present before recording an absence.

steps.title: Add a probe for each mechanically checkable row
steps.description: Extend check_audit_claims.py with a probe per row that a future edit would trip, validated by sabotage in a single shell so the file is not restored before the gate reads it. Rows that are judgment rather than text get listed as unprobed by name, and the printed row count must equal the stated total.

steps.title: Fix or report every gap
steps.description: Any row that did not land gets fixed and re-verified in the render, or reported to the author with the measurement and the reason it is blocked. Nothing is marked done from a report.

steps.title: Run persona 15 over everything changed
steps.description: Run the readability editor with its new first-read-comprehension method over every file this round touched, reading the rendered PDF after the applied-check has closed its gaps. Triage its findings and apply what is clearly right.

desired_outputs: Appendix F reworked against all 15 of the author's points, renamed to D, with each point verified in the rendered PDF or reported as not-done with the reason
The other 13 AUTHOR rulings applied or reported blocked, each verified at source
British-English and hard-phrasing rules added to WRITING_LAW/AGENT_GUARDRAILS with a gate, validated in both directions
A document-wide British-English and re-read sweep, with every hit fixed or listed for the author
PENDENCIAS.md hygienized: done items archived, section 4 removed if VERIFY_LIST is closed, file left short and easy to add to
A ledger of all 29 requested changes, each re-measured in the rendered PDF and either probed by a gate or listed as judgment, with every gap fixed or reported
Persona 15 (readability editor) run last over everything changed, with its findings triaged

feasibility.rationale: Most rulings are mechanical and verifiable in the rendered PDF. Two carry real risk: point 3 on Appendix F says the first two studies used different tasks and a different architecture, so the appendix's arc claim may need removing rather than rewording, and that is a judgment about the author's own research; and points 1 and 4 ask for citations that must be found at source or reported as not found, never invented.
